milestone: M56 Arbitrary Repository Coding Golden Journey

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: A headless caller can admit an arbitrary repository coding objective through the existing drive boundary with runtime-owned objective, index, context, and journey provenance.
Admission now requires current selected index read evidence and binds query, selection, snapshot, source event, and content hash fingerprints before the first coding task runs.
The selected context is carried into the first task.run prompt materialization while persisted journey provenance remains bounded to ids, counts, and fingerprints.
Rust validates mode permissions, freshness, replay, conflict, and fail-closed behavior; VSIX only mirrors the protocol shape.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with direct support from codebase_indexing, context_management, persistent_structured_ledger, and runtime_permission_enforcement.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive journey admission can now bind one arbitrary repository objective to validated selected index context evidence and run the admitted first coding task with that context under Rust authority.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Previously index query/read, task.run selected context, and journey admission were separate primitives; a caller could stitch them together but the runtime did not bind objective and context as one replay-safe journey admission identity.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: The Golden Journey would still begin from caller-owned context stitching with no durable runtime proof that the first coding task was admitted from current index evidence.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M55.1 atomicity and M54 technical-debt phases because this changes the objective/context admission contract and selected-context execution path.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends existing headless.run.drive, headless.run.advance, and headless.continue_once parameters only to carry the admitted selected context.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It adds bounded metadata to existing journey result/checkpoint/event structures and no new report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust prevalidates selected index evidence before task start, persists bounded objective context metadata on the journey checkpoint/event, forwards selected context to the first task.run, exact-replays the same journey, and denies conflicting objective/context replays.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A scheduled controller receives one deterministic admitted task/run and bounded next action for continuing arbitrary repository coding without inspecting raw file contents.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes the M56 entry boundary required before provider proposal, controlled apply, verification, recovery, and accepted completion slices.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive accepts one authorized journey_admission.objective_context containing bounded objective identity and selected index read evidence
stale, malformed, missing, or mismatched selected context evidence is rejected before task/checkpoint mutation
successful admission creates exactly one coding task/run and persists bounded objective/index/context provenance on the journey checkpoint and HeadlessJourneyStarted event
the first admitted task.run receives the selected index context and records summary-only prompt context materialization
exact replay returns the same task/run, journey fingerprint, and objective context metadata without duplicate task, checkpoint, drive, or ledger evidence
conflicting replay with changed objective or selected context evidence is denied before creating another task/run
no new JSON-RPC method or wrapper/report/readiness/history/digest/inspection surface is added
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_admission_binds_objective_selected_context_and_replays admits an objective with selected index evidence, runs the first task with selected context, verifies bounded metadata, and verifies exact replay

Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_admission_rejects_stale_selected_context_before_task_start mutates selected context evidence and verifies denial without task or journey checkpoint creation
Existing Rust journey admission tests continue to cover baseline admission, replay, conflict, and M55.1 rollback behavior
VSIX protocol tests accept the new objective context shape and reject raw or malformed bounded metadata

accepted_capability: Runtime-owned arbitrary repository objective context admission
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_run_drive_journey_admission -- --nocapture covers baseline, objective-context admission, exact replay, stale evidence rejection, and conflict denial
safety_boundary: reuses existing headless.run.drive, headless.run.advance, headless.continue_once, and task.run authority
validates selected index evidence before task start and again before prompt materialization
persists only bounded ids, counts, and SHA-256 fingerprints for objective context provenance
does not add provider execution, workspace mutation, shell, git, network, service control, Mode Pack activation, or product completion decisions
does not expose raw prompts, provider responses, selected file content, diffs, stdout/stderr, commands, environment, absolute paths, canonical paths, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, or secrets
non_goals: no file apply or verifier execution
rejected_alternatives: caller-side stitching of index evidence and task.start as the Golden Journey entry boundary
a new objective admission report endpoint
persisting raw selected file context in journey provenance
technical_debt: The initial selected context is forwarded through headless run-control only for the first objective-context admission step; later M56 phases should use the persisted journey task/run identity for provider proposal and apply boundaries.
Runtime lib.rs remains large and should be split only by later behavior-preserving MOVE-only refactor when it no longer competes with vertical capability work.
next_capability_rationale: M56.2 should use the admitted coding task and bounded selected context to produce one runtime-owned provider proposal candidate without applying files.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M56.1 updates current and archived phase-value manifests for the arbitrary repository objective/context admission slice. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and no wrapper/report/readiness surface was added.
